extraction_text: 维杜罗向持国王进言，指出持国王的亲友（包括毗湿摩和德罗纳）提出的建议都是为持国王好，但持国王听不进去。

attributes.relationships: 维杜罗是持国王的弟弟和谋士；毗湿摩是持国王的伯父；德罗纳是俱卢族和般度族的老师
attributes.key_point: 维杜罗强调毗湿摩和德罗纳的智慧、正直以及对持国王和般度族的同等关切

extraction_text: 维杜罗批评迦尔纳误导持国王，认为德罗纳的忠告对持国王不利。

attributes.relationships: 迦尔纳是持国王长子难敌的盟友；德罗纳是迦尔纳的敌对者
attributes.key_point: 维杜罗指出迦尔纳的短视和偏见，对比德罗纳的公正

extraction_text: 维杜罗提醒持国王，般度五子也是他的儿子，应得到公平对待。

attributes.relationships: 持国王是般度五子的伯父和监护人（因般度五子的父亲般度早逝）
attributes.key_point: 维杜罗强调家庭责任和公正，批评持国王偏袒亲生儿子难敌等

extraction_text: 维杜罗引用毗湿摩和德罗纳的警告：战胜般度五子是不可能的。

attributes.relationships: 毗湿摩和德罗纳作为军事专家预见了战争结局
attributes.key_point: 强调般度五子的无敌实力，为后续战争预言铺垫

extraction_text: 维杜罗逐一列举般度五子的超凡战力：阿周那的箭术、怖军的力量、无种和偕天的勇猛、坚战的美德。

attributes.relationships: 般度五子是兄弟，各有独特优势
attributes.supernatural_elements: 将怖军比作有万头大象之力，将无种和偕天比作阎摩之子

extraction_text: 维杜罗指出般度五子有强大盟友：大力罗摩、黑天（遮那陀那）、善战的支持。

attributes.relationships: 黑天是般度族尤其是阿周那的亲密盟友和导师；大力罗摩是黑天的哥哥；善战身份未具体说明，但被视为重要支持者
attributes.key_point: 强调般度族在战争中的绝对优势，预言其“所向无敌”

extraction_text: Vidura advises Dhritarashtra to reconcile with the Pandavas, arguing they cannot be defeated due to their alliances and righteousness.

key_points: Pandavas have right to kingdom by dharma
Alliances with Drupada and Krishna make them strong
Criticism of Duryodhana, Karna, and Shakuni

extraction_text: Dhritarashtra accepts Vidura's advice, acknowledges the Pandavas as his sons with equal rights to the kingdom, and orders their return.

key_points: Orders Vidura to bring back Pandavas, Kunti, and Draupadi

extraction_text: Vidura travels to King Drupada and the Pandavas as Dhritarashtra's envoy.

key_points: Mission to reconcile and bring Pandavas back

extraction_text: Vidura is received with honor by King Drupada and warmly greets the Pandavas and Krishna.

key_points: Affectionate greetings with Pandavas and Krishna

extraction_text: Vidura conveyed King Dhritarashtra's words, repeatedly and affectionately greeting them, and then presented them with various jewels and wealth.

attributes.relationships: Vidura acts as messenger for Dhritarashtra

extraction_text: Vidura appropriately distributed the gifts brought from the Kuru clan to the Pandava sons, Kunti, Draupadi, and the sons of King Drupada.

attributes.relationships: Vidura mediates between Kuru and Pandava/Drupada families

extraction_text: The wise Vidura humbly and politely addressed King Drupada in the presence of the Pandava sons and Krishna.

attributes.relationships: Vidura as diplomat negotiating with Drupada

extraction_text: Vidura conveyed greetings from Dhritarashtra, his princes, ministers, and relatives, expressing great joy about the marriage alliance with Drupada.

attributes.relationships: Marriage alliance between Kuru and Drupada families

extraction_text: Vidura conveyed greetings from Bhishma (son of King Shantanu) and all the Kurus, wishing Drupada well-being.

attributes.relationships: Bhishma as elder Kuru showing respect to Drupada

extraction_text: Vidura conveyed Drona's (son of Bharadvaja) affectionate embrace and greetings to his dear friend Drupada.

attributes.relationships: Drona and Drupada are close friends

extraction_text: Vidura requested Drupada to allow the five Pandava sons to return home, as all the Kurus eagerly want to see them.

attributes.relationships: Vidura negotiating Pandavas' return to Kuru kingdom

extraction_text: Vidura explained that Kunti and the Pandavas have been away from their country for a long time and must want to see their capital city.

attributes.relationships: Pandavas as exiles wanting to return home

extraction_text: Vidura stated that all Kuru women and city residents wish to see Draupadi of Panchala.

attributes.relationships: Draupadi as new bride welcomed by Kuru family

extraction_text: Vidura declared his purpose was to take the Pandavas back and promised to send a fast messenger to Dhritarashtra once Drupada consented.

attributes.relationships: Vidura as official envoy with specific mandate

extraction_text: King Drupada acknowledged Vidura's words and expressed his own happiness about the marriage alliance.

attributes.relationships: Drupada accepts diplomatic message positively

extraction_text: Drupada stated that while the noble people should return to their home, it wouldn't be appropriate for him to tell them directly.

attributes.relationships: Drupada as host respecting guests' autonomy

extraction_text: Drupada declared that if the Pandavas (Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva) wish to leave, and if Krishna and Balarama say they can go, then they may return.

attributes.relationships: Drupada defers to Pandavas' wishes and Krishna/Balarama's judgment

extraction_text: Yudhishthira declared that he and his followers are dependent on Drupada and will gladly do whatever he says.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira shows respect and deference to Drupada

extraction_text: Krishna (Vasudeva's son) expresses approval for the Pandavas' return, contingent on King Drupada's agreement.
King Drupada agrees with Krishna's assessment, acknowledging the Pandavas as relatives to both himself and Krishna.
The Pandavas, Krishna, and Vidura bid farewell to King Drupada and depart for Hastinapura with Draupadi and Kunti.
King Dhritarashtra sends a delegation including Karna, Duryodhana, Drona, and Kripa to welcome the Pandavas.
The Pandavas enter Hastinapura to great celebration from the citizens, who express joy and hope for their protection.
The Pandavas pay respects to King Dhritarashtra, Bhishma, and other elders, then enter the palace as commanded.
King Dhritarashtra proposes the Pandavas settle in the Khandava Forest to avoid conflict, offering them half the kingdom.
The Pandavas accept Dhritarashtra's proposal, receive half the kingdom, and depart for the Khandava Forest.
The Pandavas, guided by Krishna, arrived at a location and built a magnificent city resembling heaven.
The Pandavas first invited Sage Dhaumya to perform purification rituals on an auspicious plot of land, then measured the land for city construction with him.

attributes.relationships: Pandavas seek blessings from sage

extraction_text: The city was constructed with formidable defenses including moats, high walls, towers, guard posts, and various weapons.
The city featured beautiful white buildings, wide roads, and excellent urban planning to prevent disasters.

attributes.description: City described as magnificent and heavenly

extraction_text: Palaces were built for the five Pandava princes in a scenic area of the city, filled with jewels and wealth.
Brahmins proficient in Vedas and various languages came to live in the city happily.

attributes.relationships: Scholarly community establishes presence

extraction_text: Merchants and artisans from all directions came to settle in the city for profit and livelihood.

attributes.relationships: Commercial community establishes presence

extraction_text: Beautiful gardens were created around the city with numerous trees, flowers, fruits, and birds.
Pavilions, bowers, painted terraces, recreational hills, lakes, and ponds were constructed in the gardens.
The lakes and ponds featured lotuses, swans, ducks, and other waterfowl, enhancing the city's beauty.
The Pandavas lived happily in their vast territory among virtuous people.

attributes.relationships: Pandavas establish prosperous kingdom

extraction_text: The Pandavas were able to settle in the city of Indraprastha in the Khandava forest due to Bhishma and Dhritarashtra upholding dharma.

attributes.relationships: Bhishma and Dhritarashtra enable Pandavas' settlement through righteous rule

extraction_text: The five Pandavas, who were skilled in archery and resembled Indra, resided in Indraprastha, enhancing its splendor like the city of the Nagas.

attributes.action: Residence and enhancement of the city

extraction_text: Krishna, the heroic one with beautiful hair, after ensuring the Pandavas were settled, obtained their permission and returned to Dvaraka with Balarama.

attributes.relationships: Krishna and Balarama are allies and relatives of the Pandavas; Krishna is a close friend and guide to Arjuna

extraction_text: This concludes the 'Book of the Assembly Hall' (Sabha Parva) in the Mahabharata, with the next section being the 'Book of the Forest' (Aranyaka Parva).
